# EMF Dual playback and clipped text controls

Original records generated by `tools/emf_dual_clip_fixture.py`, using the
repository's independent EMF text package. No corpus artwork or font binaries
are included. The reference application exported `native.pdf` directly from `control.docx`.
`tools/record_emf_dual_clip.py` pins the source/PDF hashes and measures colored
ink and bounds at 288 DPI in two regions for each of the eight controls.

Cases cover Dual playback, equivalent plain/Dual clipped text, horizontal and
vertical cuts through glyphs, two-axis advances, anisotropic transforms, outside
and zero-width clipping rectangles. Each has a later unclipped line to detect
leaked clipping state. The first case selects an unsupported cell-height font
after the last drawing; the reference application leaves the preceding artwork intact. A unit test
also uses that font for text and verifies that unsupported rendering still fails.

The complete native/browser page pair was visually inspected. Browser tests
check all sixteen regions: empty regions have no ink; other regions remain
within 6% native ink and 0.8 pt bounds. They repeat after editing and reopening,
preserve all unrelated package parts, and verify exact undo.

Specification: MS-EMFPLUS 1.3.1 and 2.3.3.3 (Dual playback/header), MS-EMF
2.2.5 and 2.1.11 (EmrText logical clipping rectangle and ETO_CLIPPED).
These controls establish standard behavior, not a reference/spec divergence.
EMF+ Only playback, glyph-index text and drawn cell-height/rotated fonts remain
unsupported. No font-name or source-document exception is used.
